notes: Convenience/purposive Google Forms survey circulated via WhatsApp and Facebook to students of two Adamawa State polytechnics; 108 responses, no invitation count and therefore no response rate (items2-4 HIGH). Item6 HIGH: the item is a five-point agreement rating of the general statement that misleading COVID-19 information exists on social media - a perception with no external standard, and not a measure of the respondent's own exposure despite the paper's title. Item7 HIGH: no reliability or validity statistics, questionnaire not appended, the reported T-test gives only 'p = 0.05' with no statistic or df. Item10 HIGH: the denominator (108 respondents) is fine, but the numerator is an attitude-agreement share standing in for an exposure prevalence, so the numerator is not the quantity the prevalence claim implies; the 40.7% 'Agree' cell also excludes the 29.6% 'Strongly Agree'. Both 6 and 10 HIGH -> overall HIGH. Hardest call in the batch.
